description:
Burg Schlitz is a classical three-wing manor house in Hohen Demzin, in the Mecklenburgische Schweiz region of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern — a location worth stating plainly, since the name is easily and mistakenly associated with the unrelated town of Schlitz in Hesse, some 400 km away. The name instead comes from the noble family who built it, Count Hans von Schlitz, genannt von Görtz, who completed the main house in 1824 in a restrained, classical style typical of the early 19th century.

Count von Schlitz was also the designer of the estate's most distinctive feature: a 180-hectare English landscape park laid out with 36 monuments and follies, including obelisks, columns, artificial grottoes, a neo-Gothic chapel from 1822, and later sculptural additions such as a bronze fountain group from 1903. Today the manor operates as a Relais & Châteaux hotel with 20 rooms and suites furnished in period Biedermeier style, while the park itself remains freely open to the public — making Burg Schlitz one of the few properties in this directory with a substantial, independently popular visitor attraction on its own grounds.

To be entirely clear about the naming: this Burg Schlitz has no connection whatsoever to the town of Schlitz in Hesse, itself known for its own separate cluster of castles (the Schlitzer Schlösser) roughly 400 km to the south. The two places share a name purely by coincidence — one is a Mecklenburg noble family surname, the other a Hessian place name — and visitors researching either one online should take care to confirm which Schlitz, and which region of Germany, they are actually looking at.

The 180-hectare landscape park represents one of the most substantial private-estate parks in this entire collection, its scale and density of follies — 36 monuments across obelisks, columns, grottoes and a dedicated chapel — placing it closer to a designed public garden than the more modest grounds typically surrounding a German country-house hotel. Count von Schlitz's own role as the park's designer reflects the broader European aristocratic fashion for elaborate landscaped gardens during the early 19th century, when English-style naturalistic parkland design was widely adopted by continental nobility.

The park's free, unrestricted public access distinguishes Burg Schlitz from castle-hotels elsewhere in this collection where grounds access is limited to overnight guests or requires a separate paid ticket. This makes the property a genuinely worthwhile stop for visitors touring the Mecklenburg Lake District even without booking a room, a rare combination of hotel exclusivity and public-park accessibility on the same estate.

The Mecklenburgische Schweiz ("Mecklenburg Switzerland") region surrounding Hohen Demzin, named for its unusually hilly terrain by regional standards, offers a genuinely different landscape from the flat coastal plains more typically associated with Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, giving Burg Schlitz's setting a distinctive rolling, wooded character within the wider state.

The estate's Relais & Châteaux membership places it within an internationally recognized network of independently owned luxury properties, a designation that typically signals a particular commitment to regional character, individual design and quality dining — consistent with Burg Schlitz's period Biedermeier furnishings and its historically rooted, family-designed landscape park.
history: Burg Schlitz is a classical three-wing manor house completed in 1824 by Count Hans von Schlitz, genannt von Görtz, in Hohen Demzin, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern — not the town of Schlitz in Hesse, some 400 km away, with which it shares no connection beyond a coincidental name. Count von Schlitz also designed the surrounding 180-hectare English landscape park, laid out with 36 monuments and follies. Today the manor operates as a Relais & Châteaux hotel with 20 rooms in period Biedermeier style, while the park remains freely open to the public.

faqs.question: Is Burg Schlitz the same as the town of Schlitz in Hesse?
faqs.answer: No. Burg Schlitz is in Hohen Demzin, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, roughly 400 km from the unrelated town of Schlitz in Hesse. The castle's name comes from the noble Schlitz family who built it, not the Hessian place name — the two share no historical connection.

faqs.question: Can I visit the park at Burg Schlitz without staying overnight?
faqs.answer: Yes — the 180-hectare English landscape park surrounding the castle is open to the public free of charge, with 36 historic monuments and follies, guided walks, and horse-drawn carriage rides available.

faqs.question: Are all the rooms within the historic manor house?
faqs.answer: Yes — all 20 rooms and suites are within the single 1824 manor building, furnished in period Biedermeier style. There is no separate annex.

meta_description: Stay at Burg Schlitz Castle in Hohen Demzin, Mecklenburg — a classical 1824 manor with a free 180-hectare public landscape park. Not the town of Schlitz, Hesse.

hotel.non_guest_access_note: The 180-hectare Landschaftspark Burg Schlitz (English landscape park) surrounding the castle is open to the public, free of charge, for walking and hiking — it contains 36 historic monuments, follies, grottoes, and a neo-Gothic chapel (1822). Guided park walks and horse-drawn carriage rides are also available. This is a genuine, strong day-visitor draw independent of the hotel.
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** In Hohen Demzin, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern — about 30 minutes by car from Teterow or Waren (Müritz), and roughly 1.5 hours from Rostock. No direct rail access; a car is effectively required.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €169/night depending on season and room category (verify against live rate; sources vary).

**On-site:** Restaurant, spa, and the surrounding 180-hectare landscape park with guided walks and horse-drawn carriage rides; free wifi and parking included.

**Good to know:** This is Burg Schlitz in Hohen Demzin, Mecklenburg — not the town of Schlitz in Hesse. All 20 rooms are within the historic manor house itself; there is no separate annex.

**Combine with:** The Mecklenburg Lake District (Mecklenburgische Seenplatte) and the town of Teterow; the park itself is a worthwhile stop even for visitors not staying overnight.
